angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 875,191 km at 31.70 pc = 0.37 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 31.5418 +/- 0.0352 mas (same row, RUWE 0.89): 31.70 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.258 +/- 0.019 solar radii from Bonfanti et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HR 858 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...693A..90B/abstract): 875,191 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.204 +/- 0.052 solar masses from Bonfanti et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HR 858 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...693A..90B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6354 +/- 70 K from Bonfanti et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HR 858 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...693A..90B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Bonfanti et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HR 858 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...693A..90B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hr-858.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.319, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HR 858 (pscomppars): spectral type F6 V, from Gray et al. 2006 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2006AJ....132..161G/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HR 858 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.025 dex, from Bonfanti et al. 2025 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...693A..90B/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HR 858 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units 0.36361, from Bonfanti et al. 2025 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...693A..90B/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HR 858 (pscomppars): age 2 Gyr, from Bonfanti et al. 2025 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...693A..90B/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HR 858 (pscomppars): rotation period 6.7 d, from Bonfanti et al. 2025 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...693A..90B/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HR 858 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 7.5 km/s, from Bonfanti et al. 2025 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025A&A...693A..90B/abstract)
spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (1.258 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 0.790. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
